content.text:
I added transactional email to Notely using **Resend**, and wired a welcome email and a password reset email into `src/lib/users.ts`. The build, type check and lint all pass. I haven't sent a real email, because that needs a real API key and a verified sending domain.

**Why Resend:** it fits a Next.js app well. Sending is one call with a typed SDK, and delivery logs, bounces and domain setup are all in one dashboard. I followed the quickstart in `docs/resend.md`.

**Files:**
- `src/lib/resend.ts` — creates the Resend client only when it's first used. Resend throws if the API key is missing, so this keeps `next build` working without a key.
- `src/lib/email.ts` — `sendWelcomeEmail` and `sendPasswordResetEmail`. They're marked server-only, so the key can't end up in browser code. Resend returns errors instead of throwing them; these functions turn both cases into a simple success-or-error result.
- `src/emails/` — the two email templates, each with an HTML and a plain-text version. Names are escaped before they go into the HTML. I used plain functions instead of React Email so no extra template packages are needed.
- `src/lib/users.ts`:
  - **`createUser({ email, name })`** cleans up the email, rejects duplicates, adds the user and sends the welcome email. If the email fails, it's logged and signup still succeeds.
  - **`requestPasswordReset(email)`** creates a random one-time token. Only a hash of it is stored, it expires after 60 minutes, and requesting a new link cancels the old one. It then emails `${APP_URL}/reset-password?token=…`. It behaves the same whether or not the email has an account, so it can't be used to find out who is registered.
  - **`consumePasswordResetToken(token)`** checks the token, deletes it so it can't be reused, and returns the user it belongs to.
- `.env.example` — placeholder values for `RESEND_API_KEY`, `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL` and `APP_URL`. Your `.gitignore` ignored every `.env*` file, so I added an exception for `.env.example`.
- I installed two packages: `resend` and `server-only`.

**Still to do:**
- **No passwords yet:** the app doesn't store passwords. The reset flow stops at checking the token; saving the new password is up to the caller once you add password storage.
- **No pages or forms:** nothing calls these functions yet. There's no signup form, no "forgot password" form and no `/reset-password` page.
- **Data doesn't survive restarts:** users and reset tokens are kept in memory, like the existing user list.
- **To send real email:** copy `.env.example` to `.env.local`, add a real Resend key, and use a From address on a domain you've verified in Resend. For testing you can use `onboarding@resend.dev`.
